correctness.summary: A finite 12-state transfer relation exactly characterizes four-color words on each path. Endpoint K4 constraints reduce the theta problem to an exhaustive compatibility analysis, yielding all four-color obstructions. Theta(2,2,3)^2 is K6; every other obstruction has an explicit five-color witness or follows from five-color state saturation at length five. A definition-level verifier agrees on all 210 triples with 1<=a<=b<=c<=10 and b>=2.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The recent cactus classification does not treat theta graphs. Searches under theta/generalized-theta, graph-square, two-distance, distance-two, and K2,3-subdivision terminology found no exact classification of chi(Theta(a,b,c)^2). Lih--Wang--Zhu (2003) gives the general sharp K4-minor-free bound and may contain isolated theta sharpness examples; its full text was not inspected, so no novelty is claimed for the isolated K6 witness. Hetherington--Woodall (2008) is a secondary residual risk. The originality claim is the complete path-length classification and transfer proof.

value.summary: Three-path theta graphs are the simplest 2-connected non-cactus series-parallel blocks. Their exact classification shows that passing beyond cacti immediately creates infinite five-color obstruction families and a six-color case, and the transfer method is reusable for broader series-parallel square-coloring questions.

limitations: Ordinary chromatic number is classified; list chromatic number is not.
Only three-path theta graphs are treated, not generalized theta graphs with more paths.
The full texts of the two older K4-minor-free square-coloring papers were not inspected.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the general proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
